title: A systematic comparison of physics-informed neural networks and mechanistic models for epidemic modeling and forecasting
abstract: arXiv:2611.18389v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have recently been applied to epidemic modeling and forecasting with promising results. These methods integrate mechanistic knowledge with data-driven learning. Yet, their comparative performance against well-established, and simpler epidemic models is underexplored. Here, we conduct a systematic comparison of a PINN-based framework and a stochastic mechanistic model. Both approaches share the same age-structured SEIRD core and rolling-window forecasting pipeline, in a deliberately minimal setting. We evaluate their retrospective fits and probabilistic forecasts in two synthetic scenarios and the first COVID-19 wave in London. Interestingly, while PINNs underperform in synthetic scenarios, they achieve better performance on real data. translated_title: 物理信息神经网络与机理模型在流行病建模和预测中的系统性比较
translated_abstract: 物理信息神经网络近来已被应用于流行病建模和预测，并取得了令人鼓舞的成果。这些方法将机理知识与数据驱动的学习相结合。然而，它们与成熟的、更简单的流行病模型相比的性能尚未得到充分探索。在此，我们对基于PINN的框架和随机机理模型进行了系统性比较。两种方法在刻意简化的设置中共享相同的年龄分层SEIRD核心和滚动窗口预测流程。我们在两个合成场景和伦敦第一波COVID-19疫情中评估了它们的回顾性拟合和概率预测。有趣的是，虽然PINNs在合成场景中表现不佳，但它们在真实数据上取得了更好的性能。此外，PINNs在合成场景中提供了更窄的不确定性区间和更精确的参数估计。我们的研究结果证实PINNs是一种有前景的工具。
tldr: 本研究在统一的SEIRD框架下系统比较了物理信息神经网络（PINNs）与随机机理模型在流行病建模中的表现，发现PINNs虽然在合成场景中表现欠佳，但在真实COVID-19疫情数据上预测性能更优，且能提供更窄的不确定性区间和更精确的参数估计。
en_tdlr: This study systematically compares physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) with stochastic mechanistic models under a unified SEIRD framework, showing that while PINNs underperform in synthetic scenarios, they achieve better forecasting performance on real COVID-19 data with narrower uncertainty intervals and sharper parameter estimation.
